title: BBC BASIC (Z80) — R.T. Russell, on the BrickWright Z80 machine

programs.title: stored FOR/NEXT program
programs.input: 10 FOR I=1 TO 320 PRINT "Z";I30 NEXT IRUN

upstream.role: BBC BASIC (Z80) v5.00, generic CP/M edition — prebuilt by the author, shipped unmodified

notes: R.T. Russell's BBC BASIC (Z80) v5.00, the generic CP/M .COM, shipped UNMODIFIED from rtrussell/BBCZ80 (zlib). It loads at 0x0100 in the `com` slot of the bw-board Z80 machine (the same slot and path lite boots BBC BASIC on). runMediaBundle realizes the machine, loads the .COM and sets the entry PC to 0x0100; the interpreter does all console I/O through CP/M BDOS CALL 5, serviced by the minimal BDOS console shim that bw-board installs on the machine's pcTraps (the machine's own `pcTraps` comment names the CP/M BDOS console shim as its first tenant; the same shim surface is src/bbc-z80-runner.js). proof.mjs drives that real boot: it realizes the machine via runMediaBundle, installs the BDOS shim, and replays the programs[] scripted sessions (each `input` is the characters typed; `expect` is what the interpreter prints back). Because BBC BASIC flushes type-ahead after each Enter, lines are fed prompt-by-prompt (waiting for '>' before the next). The boot banner (BBC BASIC (Z80) Version 5.00 / (C) Copyright R.T.Russell 2025 / the '>' prompt) is the top-level expect[]. 'PRINT 2+2' prints the right-justified '         4'; the stored FOR/NEXT loop prints Z1/Z2/Z3. Verified reproducible: fetch.sh confirms bbcbasic.com is byte-identical to the pinned upstream binary. The name 'BBC BASIC' is used by BBC permission granted to R.T. Russell, to identify the unmodified interpreter only.
